correctness.rationale: The exact counting identity comes from two independently matching slices of the integer lecture-hall simplex. Bernoulli power sums contribute precisely B_0,B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4 and yield a four-term quartic with exact factorial normalization. For n>=5 its signs are +,+,+,- in ascending nonzero powers, so by Descartes and endpoint signs it has one simple positive root. The asymptotic follows by bracketing this root using e_j(1,...,n-1)=n^(2j)/(2^j j!)+O(n^(2j-1)). Exact rational direct enumeration/interpolation cross-checks the critical coefficient for 30 dimension/parameter combinations, and verifies the first-negative boundaries in dimensions 5 through 9. Finite checks do not substitute for the analytic theorem.

originality.rationale: The closest 2025 primary article explicitly proves only eventual negativity for each fixed dimension and tabulates first-negative values in dimensions 5–8. Its Conjecture 3.4 addresses monotonicity of overall non-positivity, which is not claimed here. The new claim gives an all-dimensional exact quartic with exactly one positive zero, exact sign threshold, and a new dimension-asymptotic scale. The 2019 structural theory yields unimodular triangulations, not monomial-coefficient thresholds; no searched record with a stronger covering implication was found. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Recent non-indexed or terminologically different literature could independently state the quartic or threshold asymptotic.
The theorem does not settle full-polynomial positivity monotonicity; that conjecture remains outside the claim.

value.rationale: The original source isolates an unbounded-dimensional family and asks about sign persistence, proves only eventual negativity, and provides the first four finite thresholds. The new claim establishes a complete sharp first-negative parameter for the first problematic coefficient in every dimension and a nontrivial n^(4/3) leading-scale law, giving substantive information across infinitely many cases without claiming the broader unsolved conjecture.
